title: Impact on Citizen Unemployment Rate When Persons who are Employed Become New Citizens
what_it_is: Impact on Citizen Unemployment Rate When Persons who are Employed Become New Citizens

sections.label: New citizens and unemployment rate
sections.summary: Adding new citizens does not significantly change the citizen unemployment rate, which is three unemployed out of 100 citizens in the labour force.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In any case, the addition of new citizens in Singapore does not change the citizen unemployment rate in any significant way.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This means, if there were only 100 citizens in the labour force, three of them are unemployed.

sections.label: Citizen unemployment rate falls
sections.summary: The citizen unemployment rate falls by 0.03 percentage points to 2.97%, and the impact of new citizens on the labour force is negligible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As a result, the citizen unemployment rate falls by 0.03 percentage points to 2.97%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In fact, out of 3.5 million Singapore Citizens, significantly less than 1% received their citizenship within the past year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Some are working adults, while others have yet to join the labour force or have retired.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This means that the impact to the citizen labour force and unemployment rate is essentially negligible.
